Hi Emma — thanks for the context and the worksheet, that helps.

Short version: we can offer two pragmatic paths and a fallback.

1) Burst bucket (temporary credits):
- Pre-purchase a capped burst credit pool for the 3-month pilot (we model'd for 1.5x peak).
- Credits drawn only for overage tokens; no long-term commit.
- Price: list rate * 0.88 (12% effective discount) for the burst bucket if purchased upfront.

2) Short-term uplift + co-term: 
- Increase committed capacity for the remainder of the year, co-terming to Dec 31 with pro-rated pricing for the remainder of the contract.
- If you lock a 6–12 month uplift (effective dates through Dec 31), we can apply a 7% uplift discount for 6-month bridge, 10% for a 12-month commit.

3) Fallback: automatic monthly true-up with a capped surcharge if usage exceeds a threshold (this avoids a PO before procurement signs off, but is higher unit price).

I'll put a draft amendment (draft_amendment_v1.pdf) and an initial pricing sheet into the thread. Ben / Rishi — can you confirm the margin/opportunity here and any SLA language we need to call out for latency in the pilot? Emma — procurement note: we can support net 30 PO for the co-term amendment; Ben will help with the commercial approval.

Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood) send a short comparison (burst credits vs 6-mo uplift) with a sample pro-rata invoice for June–Dec.
- BrightLeaf confirms whether procurement can approve a one-time burst-credit purchase now, or needs to move to a co-term amendment.

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Looping in some technical details from infra/serving so the commercials are realistic.

- For a 1.5x sustained peak across a subset of endpoints, the simplest path is a short-term dedicated burst pool that routes excess requests to a burst cluster with slightly relaxed latency SLOs (we estimate 95th p95 stable, p99 may increase by ~10–30ms under extreme load).
- If BrightLeaf needs strict p99 guarantees, we should do uplifted committed capacity (we'll pin model flavor and kernel selection to the pilot workload).

Proposed engineering-backed commercial full path (middle ground):
- 6-month uplift to Dec 31 with 7% uplift discount.
- Cap the burst credit pool at 25% of the modeled peak tokens; unused credits expire at co-term.
- SLA addendum for the pilot region: 99th percentile < 250ms for standard inference path; if we fail >3 times in a calendar month, auto-credit of 2% of monthly invoice per failure (detailed in SLA_addendum_20250618.docx).

I've attached a quick burst_calculator_20250616.xlsx that shows cost deltas for the three options (burst-only, 6-mo uplift, 12-mo uplift). Use the 'recommended' sheet for the sample pro-rata.

Rishi
